Warfarin was given only during the Feb-Mar and June 2025 admissions; outpatient notes from 7/19/2025 to 8/4/2026 list famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only, and no anticoagulant order is current. Please review whether long-term anticoagulation should be resumed.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid through 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, despite outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 documenting an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of red cells, after which apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The drug has therefore been restarted without the documented review, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the recent major GI bleed.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic note states the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was neither stopped nor removed from the medication list, and both drugs appear in that note as current. The patient is additionally on clopidogrel. Overlapping DOAC therapy carries a major haemorrhage risk and needs immediate reconciliation.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13:50 and 19:36:45) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves, markedly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19 and 0.16, RMSSD 116 ms and 98 ms) and ventricular rates of about 132 and 136/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for the 6/10/2026 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the same-day tracings and the chart should be corrected.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 5/14/2024 (current order 7/18/2026 valid to 12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 518 ms and Bazett QTc 552 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo - and it is markedly longer than the previous tracing (QTc 381 ms on 11/23/2022). The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this same ECG as "QT acceptable", which is incorrect. Latest potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Prescriber review of the QT-prolonging drug and a repeat ECG are required.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered (7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). The most recent ECG (11/24/2025, obtained 14 days after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 574 ms and Bazett QTc 583 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, and a rise of about 150 ms from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 436 ms). Latest potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: Median-beat analysis of the 3/7/2026 tracing: regular rhythm at 81/min with a discrete upright P wave before every QRS (PR 192 ms) - sinus rhythm, with mild sinus-rate variation across the strip (RR 656-856 ms). QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +37 degrees (normal). QT 346 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms at RR 744 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No earlier ECG is on file, so no comparison is possible. This is the ECG that satisfied the 14-day post-citalopram monitoring requirement.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR 578 ms, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a well-formed P wave before each QRS, PR 140 ms. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +23 degrees (normal). QT 334 ms, QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 showed regular sinus tachycardia at about 148/min with PR 132 ms and QTc 414 ms; between the two there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and only a 25 ms QTc difference. Note that this patient did have atrial fibrillation on the 2/26/2025 tracing, so paroxysmal AF is established even though the current rhythm is sinus.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular (RR 554 ms), with an identifiable P wave before each QRS and PR about 122 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +47 degrees (normal). QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 448 ms - borderline but below 500 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: no discernible P waves and irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.16, RMSSD 98 ms), mean ventricular rate about 136/min. No measurable PR interval (reported null). QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -1 degree (normal). QT 298 ms, Bazett QTc 449 ms using the mean RR. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (6/10/2026 17:13) showed the same rhythm - atrial fibrillation at about 132/min, QTc 452 ms - so there is no change between them. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing "normal sinus rhythm, rate 72" contradicts both of these tracings and is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular (RR 872 ms) with upright P waves and PR 144 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis about -28 degrees (positive lead I, near-isoelectric lead II) - at the lower limit of normal, classified NORMAL. QT 404 ms, QTc 432 ms. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 showed sinus rhythm at about 61/min with PR 160 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 422 ms; there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 10 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 614 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02), with a prominent upright P wave before each QRS and PR 124 ms. QRS 74 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +2 degrees (normal, horizontal). QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal. Only one ECG is on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR 832 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR 148 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +20 degrees (normal). QT 386 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms - normal. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026 and therefore does not satisfy the post-start monitoring requirement, which is flagged separately.

Atrial fibrillation: no P waves in any lead and markedly irregular RR intervals alternating between about 700 and 1160 ms (coefficient of variation 0.20, RMSSD 288 ms); mean ventricular rate about 61/min. No measurable PR interval (null). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +28 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad with a long tail: QT 472 ms, Bazett QTc 477 ms using the mean RR of 978 ms. The prior tracing three days earlier (11/12/2024) was sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 164 ms and QTc 391 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of about 86 ms (>=60 ms), consistent with the amiodarone loading given 11/13-11/16/2024. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 58/min with a P wave before each QRS and PR 116 ms; minor RR variation (RMSSD 42 ms) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +59 degrees (normal). QT 438 ms, Bazett QTc 432 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 3/8/2025 was essentially identical (sinus 62/min, PR 116 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 452 ms), so no changes: no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new block and a QTc difference of 20 ms. Note this tracing predates the haloperidol start of 9/15/2026; a new baseline ECG is required.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, very regular (RR 721 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00), with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 152 ms. QRS 72 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms - normal. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 76/min, regular, with a large upright P wave before each QRS and PR 166 ms. QRS 68 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +62 degrees (normal). QT 432 ms, Bazett QTc 488 ms - still borderline but below 500 ms. The prior tracing of 2/2/2020 had a grossly prolonged QT (556 ms) with Bazett QTc 620 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 132 ms (>=60 ms), a substantial improvement. No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, perfectly regular (RR 498 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00) with a clear P wave before each QRS; PR 196 ms (upper normal, no AV block). QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +51 degrees (normal). QT 290 ms, QTc 411 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 184 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 413 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and a QTc difference of only 2 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular (RR 1101 ms), with an upright P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is prolonged at about 222 ms with 1:1 conduction - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis about +1 degree (lead I upright, aVF nearly isoelectric) - normal. QT 416 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 51/min with PR 194 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc 387 ms; there is no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 10 ms, so no listed change categories apply (the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no organised atrial activity and irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms); mean ventricular rate about 151/min. No measurable PR interval (null). QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -23 degrees (normal). QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The tracing from the previous evening (9/12/2025) also showed atrial fibrillation, at about 77/min with QTc 434 ms, so the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc difference is only 4 ms; the ventricular rate has accelerated markedly, which is what prompted the intravenous amiodarone given later that day. He is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 174 ms; slight RR variability (RMSSD 35 ms) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +1 degree (normal). QT 364 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 had a markedly prolonged QT (520 ms) with QTc 549 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 150 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. The 11/23/2025 clinic note describing "ECG today: sinus rhythm" is consistent with this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS; PR about 194 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +54 degrees (normal). QT 388 ms, Bazett QTc 431 ms - normal. The tracing carries some high-frequency noise but the measurements are reliable on the signal-averaged beat. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, metronomically regular (RR 538 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00), with a discrete upright P wave in II/III/aVF before every QRS (PR 176 ms) - not atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +32 degrees (normal). Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy are met (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) with secondary ST-T changes. QT 314 ms, Bazett QTc 428 ms. The prior tracing of 7/4/2022 was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 428 ms), so there are no changes. Atrial flutter was coded in September 2025 but is not present on this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at about 62/min with an upright, somewhat broad P wave before each conducted QRS and a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not clearly first-degree AV block). The RR series (984, 984, 540, 1370, 996, 968, 936, 980, 978 ms) shows one early beat with a compensatory pause - an isolated ectopic - on an otherwise regular sinus rhythm; this is not atrial fibrillation, since a consistent P wave precedes each sinus beat. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -35 degrees (positive I and aVL, negative II/III/aVF) - left axis deviation. QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only one ECG is on file. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded at this same encounter, and sinus rhythm on this tracing does not exclude it.

Regular rhythm at 70/min with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS at PR 150 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal plane is highly unusual: QRS is deeply negative in I (-1.4 mV) and II, positive in aVR, and slightly negative in aVF, giving a measured axis of about -172 degrees (EXTREME / north-west quadrant); the P wave is likewise negative in I and aVL and positive in aVR while the precordial leads show entirely normal R-wave progression. This pattern is characteristic of left/right arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms - normal (reassuring, since this ECG followed the escitalopram start, although it was done 19 days after the start rather than within the required 14 days). No prior ECG is available.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 160 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +38 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, low-amplitude T wave: QT 530 ms at RR 858 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 574 ms - well above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QTc 442 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 130 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. Marked QT prolongation in a 35-year-old woman taking citalopram 40 mg daily - flagged separately for urgent prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 878 ms), with a clear upright P wave before each QRS and PR 150 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +71 degrees (normal, vertical). QT 436 ms, Bazett QTc 465 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold, and acceptable on escitalopram; worth re-checking if the dose is increased or another QT-prolonging drug is added. No prior ECG is on file. This tracing satisfied the 30-day post-escitalopram monitoring requirement.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 182 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -10 degrees (normal). QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66/min with PR 172 ms, QRS 94 ms and QTc 406 ms; there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of about 31 ms, so no change categories apply.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, upright P waves with PR about 150 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +36 degrees (normal). The T wave is markedly prolonged and broad: QT 518 ms at RR 880 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 552 ms - clearly above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 11/23/2022 had QTc 381 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 170 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. This marked QT prolongation in a patient on escitalopram is flagged separately for prescriber review; the 5/14/2024 note describing this ECG as having an acceptable QT is inaccurate.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast and strikingly regular (RR 402-454 ms, mean 426 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02, rate about 141/min) and there are no discrete sinus P waves; instead, regular atrial deflections of identical morphology recur every ~210 ms (atrial rate about 285/min) - one buried in the ST segment and one in the T-P segment of each cycle, giving the characteristic saw-tooth baseline best seen in II, III and V1. There is therefore no measurable PR interval (null). QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -3 degrees (normal). QT 268 ms, Bazett QTc 410 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, RMSSD 190 ms, no atrial organisation), so the atrial fibrillation has resolved and organised into new atrial flutter; QTc is essentially unchanged (425 to 410 ms). He is currently on two overlapping anticoagulants, which is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR 735 ms), with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 172 ms. QRS 100 ms - mildly widened, a non-specific intraventricular conduction delay, but below 120 ms and without an RBBB or LBBB pattern, so no bundle branch block is coded. Frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 445 ms - borderline, below 500 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, very regular (RR 659 ms), with an upright P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is clearly prolonged at about 248 ms with 1:1 conduction - first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -17 degrees (normal). QT 356 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing of 5/16/2021 showed sinus rhythm at 87/min with a normal PR of 150 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 418 ms; AV conduction has therefore slowed since then, but none of the listed change categories apply (no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block, QTc difference only 21 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 496 ms, coefficient of variation 0.01), with a P wave preceding each QRS and PR 138 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +65 degrees (normal, vertical). QT 312 ms with Bazett QTc 443 ms - borderline only as an artefact of Bazett over-correction at this rate; the absolute QT is normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with clear P waves and PR 154 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms, QTc 445 ms. The immediately preceding tracing from the same morning (10:06:50, 100/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 429 ms) is essentially identical, so there are no changes: no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new conduction block and a QTc difference of 16 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1150 ms), upright P waves with PR 180 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). Large precordial voltages. QT 450 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc 417 ms (normal). The prior tracing of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm at about 58/min (PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 410 ms) with a single early beat and compensatory pause; no changes between the two - no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 7 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, metronomically regular (RR 494 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR 134 ms. QRS is now narrow at 90 ms. Frontal QRS axis is about +177 degrees (rS in I and aVL, qR in III, aVF near isoelectric) - a rightward/indeterminate axis, classified RIGHT. QT 312 ms, QTc 444 ms. The earlier tracing from the same day (12/5/2024 01:33) showed sinus rhythm at 100/min with QRS 150 ms and an rSR-prime in V1 with broad terminal R and wide S waves in I, V5 and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, so the QRS has normalised. QTc fell from about 505 to 444 ms, but that difference is almost entirely accounted for by the 60 ms of QRS narrowing and lies within measurement uncertainty of the 60 ms threshold, so I have not coded a QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (RR 968 ms) with upright P waves, PR about 176 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +67 degrees (normal). There is gross repolarisation prolongation with a very broad low T wave: QT 574 ms, Bazett QTc 583 ms - far above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 6/7/2025, before amiodarone was started, showed sinus rhythm about 49/min with QTc 436 ms, so the QTc has risen by roughly 150 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. Amiodarone-related QT prolongation; flagged separately for prescriber review.

Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves anywhere in the cycle (the T-P segment is flat at baseline) and grossly irregular RR intervals ranging 386-1092 ms (coefficient of variation 0.29, RMSSD 264 ms). Mean ventricular rate about 101/min. There is no measurable PR interval, so PR is reported as null. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -61 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 334 ms with Bazett QTc 433 ms using the mean RR. No prior ECG is on file for comparison. The patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at about 59/min, with an upright P wave before each QRS and a prolonged PR of about 210 ms - first-degree AV block. The QRS is wide at 130 ms with a broad monophasic R wave and late intrinsicoid deflection in I, aVL and V6, deep wide S/QS complexes in V1-V4 and no septal q waves laterally - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -23 degrees, within normal limits (lead I strongly positive, lead II net positive). QT 448 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms using the mean RR of 1019 ms - appropriately prolonged for the wide QRS. The prior tracing of 6/3/2024 showed the same pattern (sinus about 68/min, PR 228 ms, QRS 128 ms, identical LBBB morphology, QTc 457 ms), so nothing has changed: the bundle branch block is pre-existing rather than new, and the QTc difference is only 13 ms.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in serial Cardiology Clinic notes (9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, diabetes, prior TIA/cerebral infarction = 2, coronary atherosclerosis/old MI, female). She received dabigatran, then rivaroxaban, then apixaban during the January 2025 admission, but all were stopped by 2/3/2025 and every clinic note since lists only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin - no anticoagulant is current as of 9/24/2026. Guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation is absent; needs review.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 10/2/2023 (current order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027); 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised with citalopram in patients at risk. The most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 530 ms and Bazett QTc 574 ms, above the 500 ms threshold, and much longer than the prior tracing (QTc 442 ms, 6/17/2020). Latest potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of the dose and a current ECG are required.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 3/1/2022 (current order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 592 ms and Bazett QTc 581 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, up from QTc 474 ms on the atrial fibrillation tracing three weeks earlier. Latest potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. She is also on warfarin (dose just reduced) and metoprolol. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025, i.e. on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 583 ms and is the subject of a separate QT_SAFETY item.)

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 402 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the earlier 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 465 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start - so it falls outside the required window and the requirement was not met in time. (That tracing was reassuring: sinus rhythm, QTc 409 ms.) Due date has passed, so the monitoring requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (order valid to 12/26/2026); a brief inpatient course in December 2025 had ended, so this is a new start. The revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 8/1/2026 - the only tracing in the chart is from 12/25/2025 - and no outside result is referenced, so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and would satisfy the requirement, but it is not in the chart, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since (the most recent tracing is 3/9/2025), but the deadline is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due. A baseline ECG should be scheduled promptly, particularly as she also has chronic kidney disease.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 8/22/2025 and carried in the history of every Cardiology Clinic note through 6/27/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered; current medications are levothyroxine only (previously tamsulosin). Score >=2 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of therapy needs review. Note the coded history of "hemorrhage complicating a procedure" (2025) should be weighed in the bleeding-risk discussion.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD), acting under the clinic standing order, decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 6/17/2026 (INR 2.7); the 3.4 value was a home reading that prompted the change rather than follow-up testing. The follow-up INR is therefore overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 3/14/2025 at the admission for cardioembolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke = 2, hypertension, age 65-74, female). Her ECG of 3/14/2025 was in sinus rhythm, which is expected in paroxysmal AF and does not remove the indication. Current medications in all clinic notes through 6/23/2026 are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine - no anticoagulant is ordered (only a single inpatient subcutaneous heparin dose on 3/17/2025). Class 1 anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention is missing; needs review (thrombocytopenia coded 3/2025 should be rechecked before starting).

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in the history of every Cardiology Clinic note and confirmed on the ECG of 2/26/2025 (irregularly irregular, no P waves, ventricular rate ~167). CHA2DS2-VASc 2: congestive heart failure (acute systolic heart failure / congestive heart failure / other primary cardiomyopathy coded 2/26/2025) plus hypertension; age 48 and male contribute 0. A score of 2 meets the Class 1 threshold for oral anticoagulation. Warfarin was given only during the Feb-Mar and June 2025 admissions; outpatient notes from 7/19/2025 to 8/4/2026 list famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only, and no anticoagulant order is current. Please review whether long-term anticoagulation should be resumed.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid through 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, despite outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 documenting an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of red cells, after which apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The drug has therefore been restarted without the documented review, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the recent major GI bleed.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic note states the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was neither stopped nor removed from the medication list, and both drugs appear in that note as current. The patient is additionally on clopidogrel. Overlapping DOAC therapy carries a major haemorrhage risk and needs immediate reconciliation.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13:50 and 19:36:45) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves, markedly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19 and 0.16, RMSSD 116 ms and 98 ms) and ventricular rates of about 132 and 136/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for the 6/10/2026 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the same-day tracings and the chart should be corrected.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 5/14/2024 (current order 7/18/2026 valid to 12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 518 ms and Bazett QTc 552 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo - and it is markedly longer than the previous tracing (QTc 381 ms on 11/23/2022). The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this same ECG as "QT acceptable", which is incorrect. Latest potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Prescriber review of the QT-prolonging drug and a repeat ECG are required.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered (7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). The most recent ECG (11/24/2025, obtained 14 days after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 574 ms and Bazett QTc 583 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, and a rise of about 150 ms from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 436 ms). Latest potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: Median-beat analysis of the 3/7/2026 tracing: regular rhythm at 81/min with a discrete upright P wave before every QRS (PR 192 ms) - sinus rhythm, with mild sinus-rate variation across the strip (RR 656-856 ms). QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +37 degrees (normal). QT 346 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms at RR 744 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No earlier ECG is on file, so no comparison is possible. This is the ECG that satisfied the 14-day post-citalopram monitoring requirement.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR 578 ms, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a well-formed P wave before each QRS, PR 140 ms. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +23 degrees (normal). QT 334 ms, QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 showed regular sinus tachycardia at about 148/min with PR 132 ms and QTc 414 ms; between the two there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and only a 25 ms QTc difference. Note that this patient did have atrial fibrillation on the 2/26/2025 tracing, so paroxysmal AF is established even though the current rhythm is sinus.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular (RR 554 ms), with an identifiable P wave before each QRS and PR about 122 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +47 degrees (normal). QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 448 ms - borderline but below 500 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: no discernible P waves and irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.16, RMSSD 98 ms), mean ventricular rate about 136/min. No measurable PR interval (reported null). QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -1 degree (normal). QT 298 ms, Bazett QTc 449 ms using the mean RR. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (6/10/2026 17:13) showed the same rhythm - atrial fibrillation at about 132/min, QTc 452 ms - so there is no change between them. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing "normal sinus rhythm, rate 72" contradicts both of these tracings and is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular (RR 872 ms) with upright P waves and PR 144 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis about -28 degrees (positive lead I, near-isoelectric lead II) - at the lower limit of normal, classified NORMAL. QT 404 ms, QTc 432 ms. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 showed sinus rhythm at about 61/min with PR 160 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 422 ms; there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 10 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 614 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02), with a prominent upright P wave before each QRS and PR 124 ms. QRS 74 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +2 degrees (normal, horizontal). QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal. Only one ECG is on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR 832 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR 148 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +20 degrees (normal). QT 386 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms - normal. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026 and therefore does not satisfy the post-start monitoring requirement, which is flagged separately.

Atrial fibrillation: no P waves in any lead and markedly irregular RR intervals alternating between about 700 and 1160 ms (coefficient of variation 0.20, RMSSD 288 ms); mean ventricular rate about 61/min. No measurable PR interval (null). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +28 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad with a long tail: QT 472 ms, Bazett QTc 477 ms using the mean RR of 978 ms. The prior tracing three days earlier (11/12/2024) was sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 164 ms and QTc 391 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of about 86 ms (>=60 ms), consistent with the amiodarone loading given 11/13-11/16/2024. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 58/min with a P wave before each QRS and PR 116 ms; minor RR variation (RMSSD 42 ms) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +59 degrees (normal). QT 438 ms, Bazett QTc 432 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 3/8/2025 was essentially identical (sinus 62/min, PR 116 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 452 ms), so no changes: no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new block and a QTc difference of 20 ms. Note this tracing predates the haloperidol start of 9/15/2026; a new baseline ECG is required.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, very regular (RR 721 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00), with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 152 ms. QRS 72 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms - normal. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 76/min, regular, with a large upright P wave before each QRS and PR 166 ms. QRS 68 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +62 degrees (normal). QT 432 ms, Bazett QTc 488 ms - still borderline but below 500 ms. The prior tracing of 2/2/2020 had a grossly prolonged QT (556 ms) with Bazett QTc 620 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 132 ms (>=60 ms), a substantial improvement. No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, perfectly regular (RR 498 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00) with a clear P wave before each QRS; PR 196 ms (upper normal, no AV block). QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +51 degrees (normal). QT 290 ms, QTc 411 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 184 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 413 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and a QTc difference of only 2 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular (RR 1101 ms), with an upright P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is prolonged at about 222 ms with 1:1 conduction - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis about +1 degree (lead I upright, aVF nearly isoelectric) - normal. QT 416 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 51/min with PR 194 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc 387 ms; there is no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 10 ms, so no listed change categories apply (the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no organised atrial activity and irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms); mean ventricular rate about 151/min. No measurable PR interval (null). QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -23 degrees (normal). QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The tracing from the previous evening (9/12/2025) also showed atrial fibrillation, at about 77/min with QTc 434 ms, so the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc difference is only 4 ms; the ventricular rate has accelerated markedly, which is what prompted the intravenous amiodarone given later that day. He is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 174 ms; slight RR variability (RMSSD 35 ms) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +1 degree (normal). QT 364 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 had a markedly prolonged QT (520 ms) with QTc 549 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 150 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. The 11/23/2025 clinic note describing "ECG today: sinus rhythm" is consistent with this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS; PR about 194 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +54 degrees (normal). QT 388 ms, Bazett QTc 431 ms - normal. The tracing carries some high-frequency noise but the measurements are reliable on the signal-averaged beat. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, metronomically regular (RR 538 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00), with a discrete upright P wave in II/III/aVF before every QRS (PR 176 ms) - not atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +32 degrees (normal). Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy are met (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) with secondary ST-T changes. QT 314 ms, Bazett QTc 428 ms. The prior tracing of 7/4/2022 was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 428 ms), so there are no changes. Atrial flutter was coded in September 2025 but is not present on this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at about 62/min with an upright, somewhat broad P wave before each conducted QRS and a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not clearly first-degree AV block). The RR series (984, 984, 540, 1370, 996, 968, 936, 980, 978 ms) shows one early beat with a compensatory pause - an isolated ectopic - on an otherwise regular sinus rhythm; this is not atrial fibrillation, since a consistent P wave precedes each sinus beat. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -35 degrees (positive I and aVL, negative II/III/aVF) - left axis deviation. QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only one ECG is on file. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded at this same encounter, and sinus rhythm on this tracing does not exclude it.

Regular rhythm at 70/min with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS at PR 150 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal plane is highly unusual: QRS is deeply negative in I (-1.4 mV) and II, positive in aVR, and slightly negative in aVF, giving a measured axis of about -172 degrees (EXTREME / north-west quadrant); the P wave is likewise negative in I and aVL and positive in aVR while the precordial leads show entirely normal R-wave progression. This pattern is characteristic of left/right arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms - normal (reassuring, since this ECG followed the escitalopram start, although it was done 19 days after the start rather than within the required 14 days). No prior ECG is available.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 160 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +38 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, low-amplitude T wave: QT 530 ms at RR 858 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 574 ms - well above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QTc 442 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 130 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. Marked QT prolongation in a 35-year-old woman taking citalopram 40 mg daily - flagged separately for urgent prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 878 ms), with a clear upright P wave before each QRS and PR 150 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +71 degrees (normal, vertical). QT 436 ms, Bazett QTc 465 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold, and acceptable on escitalopram; worth re-checking if the dose is increased or another QT-prolonging drug is added. No prior ECG is on file. This tracing satisfied the 30-day post-escitalopram monitoring requirement.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 182 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -10 degrees (normal). QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66/min with PR 172 ms, QRS 94 ms and QTc 406 ms; there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of about 31 ms, so no change categories apply.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, upright P waves with PR about 150 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +36 degrees (normal). The T wave is markedly prolonged and broad: QT 518 ms at RR 880 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 552 ms - clearly above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 11/23/2022 had QTc 381 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 170 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. This marked QT prolongation in a patient on escitalopram is flagged separately for prescriber review; the 5/14/2024 note describing this ECG as having an acceptable QT is inaccurate.

Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast and strikingly regular (RR 402-454 ms, mean 426 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02, rate about 141/min) and there are no discrete sinus P waves; instead, regular atrial deflections of identical morphology recur every ~210 ms (atrial rate about 285/min) - one buried in the ST segment and one in the T-P segment of each cycle, giving the characteristic saw-tooth baseline best seen in II, III and V1. There is therefore no measurable PR interval (null). QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -3 degrees (normal). QT 268 ms, Bazett QTc 410 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, RMSSD 190 ms, no atrial organisation), so the atrial fibrillation has resolved and organised into new atrial flutter; QTc is essentially unchanged (425 to 410 ms). He is currently on two overlapping anticoagulants, which is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR 735 ms), with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 172 ms. QRS 100 ms - mildly widened, a non-specific intraventricular conduction delay, but below 120 ms and without an RBBB or LBBB pattern, so no bundle branch block is coded. Frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 445 ms - borderline, below 500 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, very regular (RR 659 ms), with an upright P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is clearly prolonged at about 248 ms with 1:1 conduction - first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -17 degrees (normal). QT 356 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing of 5/16/2021 showed sinus rhythm at 87/min with a normal PR of 150 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 418 ms; AV conduction has therefore slowed since then, but none of the listed change categories apply (no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block, QTc difference only 21 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 496 ms, coefficient of variation 0.01), with a P wave preceding each QRS and PR 138 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis +65 degrees (normal, vertical). QT 312 ms with Bazett QTc 443 ms - borderline only as an artefact of Bazett over-correction at this rate; the absolute QT is normal. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with clear P waves and PR 154 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms, QTc 445 ms. The immediately preceding tracing from the same morning (10:06:50, 100/min, PR 152 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 429 ms) is essentially identical, so there are no changes: no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new conduction block and a QTc difference of 16 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1150 ms), upright P waves with PR 180 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). Large precordial voltages. QT 450 ms at this slow rate, Bazett QTc 417 ms (normal). The prior tracing of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm at about 58/min (PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 410 ms) with a single early beat and compensatory pause; no changes between the two - no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 7 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, metronomically regular (RR 494 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR 134 ms. QRS is now narrow at 90 ms. Frontal QRS axis is about +177 degrees (rS in I and aVL, qR in III, aVF near isoelectric) - a rightward/indeterminate axis, classified RIGHT. QT 312 ms, QTc 444 ms. The earlier tracing from the same day (12/5/2024 01:33) showed sinus rhythm at 100/min with QRS 150 ms and an rSR-prime in V1 with broad terminal R and wide S waves in I, V5 and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, so the QRS has normalised. QTc fell from about 505 to 444 ms, but that difference is almost entirely accounted for by the 60 ms of QRS narrowing and lies within measurement uncertainty of the 60 ms threshold, so I have not coded a QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (RR 968 ms) with upright P waves, PR about 176 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +67 degrees (normal). There is gross repolarisation prolongation with a very broad low T wave: QT 574 ms, Bazett QTc 583 ms - far above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 6/7/2025, before amiodarone was started, showed sinus rhythm about 49/min with QTc 436 ms, so the QTc has risen by roughly 150 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. Amiodarone-related QT prolongation; flagged separately for prescriber review.

Atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves anywhere in the cycle (the T-P segment is flat at baseline) and grossly irregular RR intervals ranging 386-1092 ms (coefficient of variation 0.29, RMSSD 264 ms). Mean ventricular rate about 101/min. There is no measurable PR interval, so PR is reported as null. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -61 degrees (left axis deviation). QT 334 ms with Bazett QTc 433 ms using the mean RR. No prior ECG is on file for comparison. The patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in serial Cardiology Clinic notes (9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, diabetes, prior TIA/cerebral infarction = 2, coronary atherosclerosis/old MI, female). She received dabigatran, then rivaroxaban, then apixaban during the January 2025 admission, but all were stopped by 2/3/2025 and every clinic note since lists only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin - no anticoagulant is current as of 9/24/2026. Guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation is absent; needs review.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 10/2/2023 (current order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027); 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised with citalopram in patients at risk. The most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 530 ms and Bazett QTc 574 ms, above the 500 ms threshold, and much longer than the prior tracing (QTc 442 ms, 6/17/2020). Latest potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of the dose and a current ECG are required.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 3/1/2022 (current order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027). Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 592 ms and Bazett QTc 581 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, up from QTc 474 ms on the atrial fibrillation tracing three weeks earlier. Latest potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. She is also on warfarin (dose just reduced) and metoprolol. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025, i.e. on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 583 ms and is the subject of a separate QT_SAFETY item.)

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 402 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the earlier 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 465 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start - so it falls outside the required window and the requirement was not met in time. (That tracing was reassuring: sinus rhythm, QTc 409 ms.) Due date has passed, so the monitoring requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (order valid to 12/26/2026); a brief inpatient course in December 2025 had ended, so this is a new start. The revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 8/1/2026 - the only tracing in the chart is from 12/25/2025 - and no outside result is referenced, so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and would satisfy the requirement, but it is not in the chart, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since (the most recent tracing is 3/9/2025), but the deadline is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due. A baseline ECG should be scheduled promptly, particularly as she also has chronic kidney disease.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 8/22/2025 and carried in the history of every Cardiology Clinic note through 6/27/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No anticoagulant has ever been ordered; current medications are levothyroxine only (previously tamsulosin). Score >=2 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of therapy needs review. Note the coded history of "hemorrhage complicating a procedure" (2025) should be weighed in the bleeding-risk discussion.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD), acting under the clinic standing order, decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 6/17/2026 (INR 2.7); the 3.4 value was a home reading that prompted the change rather than follow-up testing. The follow-up INR is therefore overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 3/14/2025 at the admission for cardioembolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke = 2, hypertension, age 65-74, female). Her ECG of 3/14/2025 was in sinus rhythm, which is expected in paroxysmal AF and does not remove the indication. Current medications in all clinic notes through 6/23/2026 are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine - no anticoagulant is ordered (only a single inpatient subcutaneous heparin dose on 3/17/2025). Class 1 anticoagulation for secondary stroke prevention is missing; needs review (thrombocytopenia coded 3/2025 should be rechecked before starting).

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in the history of every Cardiology Clinic note and confirmed on the ECG of 2/26/2025 (irregularly irregular, no P waves, ventricular rate ~167). CHA2DS2-VASc 2: congestive heart failure (acute systolic heart failure / congestive heart failure / other primary cardiomyopathy coded 2/26/2025) plus hypertension; age 48 and male contribute 0. A score of 2 meets the Class 1 threshold for oral anticoagulation. Warfarin was given only during the Feb-Mar and June 2025 admissions; outpatient notes from 7/19/2025 to 8/4/2026 list famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only, and no anticoagulant order is current. Please review whether long-term anticoagulation should be resumed.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid through 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, despite outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 documenting an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of red cells, after which apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The drug has therefore been restarted without the documented review, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the recent major GI bleed.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 1/3/2027). Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular (RR 1101 ms), with an upright P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is prolonged at about 222 ms with 1:1 conduction - first-degree AV block. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no organised atrial activity and irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms); mean ventricular rate about 151/min. He is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 174 ms; slight RR variability (RMSSD 35 ms) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS; PR about 194 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block. The tracing carries some high-frequency noise but the measurements are reliable on the signal-averaged beat. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, metronomically regular (RR 538 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00), with a discrete upright P wave in II/III/aVF before every QRS (PR 176 ms) - not atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +32 degrees (normal). Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy are met (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) with secondary ST-T changes. QT 314 ms, Bazett QTc 428 ms. The prior tracing of 7/4/2022 was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 428 ms), so there are no changes. Atrial flutter was coded in September 2025 but is not present on this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at about 62/min with an upright, somewhat broad P wave before each conducted QRS and a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not clearly first-degree AV block). The RR series (984, 984, 540, 1370, 996, 968, 936, 980, 978 ms) shows one early beat with a compensatory pause - an isolated ectopic - on an otherwise regular sinus rhythm; this is not atrial fibrillation, since a consistent P wave precedes each sinus beat. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -35 degrees (positive I and aVL, negative II/III/aVF) - left axis deviation. QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only one ECG is on file. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded at this same encounter, and sinus rhythm on this tracing does not exclude it.

Regular rhythm at 70/min with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS at PR 150 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal plane is highly unusual: QRS is deeply negative in I (-1.4 mV) and II, positive in aVR, and slightly negative in aVF, giving a measured axis of about -172 degrees (EXTREME / north-west quadrant); the P wave is likewise negative in I and aVL and positive in aVR while the precordial leads show entirely normal R-wave progression. This pattern is characteristic of left/right arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms - normal (reassuring, since this ECG followed the escitalopram start, although it was done 19 days after the start rather than within the required 14 days). No prior ECG is available.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 160 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +38 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, low-amplitude T wave: QT 530 ms at RR 858 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 574 ms - well above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QTc 442 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 130 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. Marked QT prolongation in a 35-year-old woman taking citalopram 40 mg daily - flagged separately for urgent prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 878 ms), with a clear upright P wave before each QRS and PR 150 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +71 degrees (normal, vertical). Atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. The ventricular response is fast and strikingly regular (RR 402-454 ms, mean 426 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02, rate about 141/min) and there are no discrete sinus P waves; instead, regular atrial deflections of identical morphology recur every ~210 ms (atrial rate about 285/min) - one buried in the ST segment and one in the T-P segment of each cycle, giving the characteristic saw-tooth baseline best seen in II, III and V1. There is therefore no measurable PR interval (null). QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -3 degrees (normal). QT 268 ms, Bazett QTc 410 ms. The prior tracing of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, RMSSD 190 ms, no atrial organisation), so the atrial fibrillation has resolved and organised into new atrial flutter; QTc is essentially unchanged (425 to 410 ms). He is currently on two overlapping anticoagulants, which is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR 735 ms), with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 172 ms. Frontal axis +35 degrees (normal). QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 445 ms - borderline, below 500 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min, very regular (RR 659 ms), with an upright P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is clearly prolonged at about 248 ms with 1:1 conduction - first-degree AV block. 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 8/22/2025 and carried in the history of every Cardiology Clinic note through 6/27/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). Warfarin was given only during the Feb-Mar and June 2025 admissions; outpatient notes from 7/19/2025 to 8/4/2026 list famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only, and no anticoagulant order is current. Please review whether long-term anticoagulation should be resumed.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid through 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, despite outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 documenting an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of red cells, after which apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The drug has therefore been restarted without the documented review, and the patient is also on aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, compounding bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review of the recent major GI bleed.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 Cardiology Clinic note states the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was neither stopped nor removed from the medication list, and both drugs appear in that note as current. The patient is additionally on clopidogrel. Overlapping DOAC therapy carries a major haemorrhage risk and needs immediate reconciliation.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13:50 and 19:36:45) show atrial fibrillation: no organised P waves, markedly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19 and 0.16, RMSSD 116 ms and 98 ms) and ventricular rates of about 132 and 136/min. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for the 6/10/2026 encounter and warfarin was started. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the same-day tracings and the chart should be corrected.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 5/14/2024 (current order 7/18/2026 valid to 12/26/2026). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 518 ms and Bazett QTc 552 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo - and it is markedly longer than the previous tracing (QTc 381 ms on 11/23/2022). The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this same ECG as "QT acceptable", which is incorrect. Latest potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are low-normal. Prescriber review of the QT-prolonging drug and a repeat ECG are required.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered (7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). The most recent ECG (11/24/2025, obtained 14 days after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 574 ms and Bazett QTc 583 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, and a rise of about 150 ms from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 436 ms). Latest potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: Median-beat analysis of the 3/7/2026 tracing: regular rhythm at 81/min with a discrete upright P wave before every QRS (PR 192 ms) - sinus rhythm, with mild sinus-rate variation across the strip (RR 656-856 ms). QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +37 degrees (normal). QT 346 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms at RR 744 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No earlier ECG is on file, so no comparison is possible. This is the ECG that satisfied the 14-day post-citalopram monitoring requirement.

Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR 578 ms, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a well-formed P wave before each QRS, PR 140 ms. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +23 degrees (normal). QT 334 ms, QTc 439 ms. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 showed regular sinus tachycardia at about 148/min with PR 132 ms and QTc 414 ms; between the two there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and only a 25 ms QTc difference. Note that this patient did have atrial fibrillation on the 2/26/2025 tracing, so paroxysmal AF is established even though the current rhythm is sinus.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 108/min, regular (RR 554 ms), with an identifiable P wave before each QRS and PR about 122 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +47 degrees (normal). QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 448 ms - borderline but below 500 ms. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: no discernible P waves and irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.16, RMSSD 98 ms), mean ventricular rate about 136/min. No measurable PR interval (reported null). QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -1 degree (normal). QT 298 ms, Bazett QTc 449 ms using the mean RR. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (6/10/2026 17:13) showed the same rhythm - atrial fibrillation at about 132/min, QTc 452 ms - so there is no change between them. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing "normal sinus rhythm, rate 72" contradicts both of these tracings and is flagged separately.

Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular (RR 872 ms) with upright P waves and PR 144 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis about -28 degrees (positive lead I, near-isoelectric lead II) - at the lower limit of normal, classified NORMAL. QT 404 ms, QTc 432 ms. The prior tracing of 4/27/2025 showed sinus rhythm at about 61/min with PR 160 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc 422 ms; there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 10 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 98/min, regular (RR 614 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02), with a prominent upright P wave before each QRS and PR 124 ms. QRS 74 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +2 degrees (normal, horizontal). QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal. Only one ECG is on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR 832 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR 148 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +20 degrees (normal). QT 386 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms - normal. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible. It predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026 and therefore does not satisfy the post-start monitoring requirement, which is flagged separately.

Atrial fibrillation: no P waves in any lead and markedly irregular RR intervals alternating between about 700 and 1160 ms (coefficient of variation 0.20, RMSSD 288 ms); mean ventricular rate about 61/min. No measurable PR interval (null). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +28 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad with a long tail: QT 472 ms, Bazett QTc 477 ms using the mean RR of 978 ms. The prior tracing three days earlier (11/12/2024) was sinus rhythm at 69/min with PR 164 ms and QTc 391 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of about 86 ms (>=60 ms), consistent with the amiodarone loading given 11/13-11/16/2024. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 58/min with a P wave before each QRS and PR 116 ms; minor RR variation (RMSSD 42 ms) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +59 degrees (normal). QT 438 ms, Bazett QTc 432 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 3/8/2025 was essentially identical (sinus 62/min, PR 116 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 452 ms), so no changes: no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new block and a QTc difference of 20 ms. Note this tracing predates the haloperidol start of 9/15/2026; a new baseline ECG is required.

Sinus rhythm at 83/min, very regular (RR 721 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00), with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 152 ms. QRS 72 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms - normal. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 76/min, regular, with a large upright P wave before each QRS and PR 166 ms. QRS 68 ms, narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +62 degrees (normal). QT 432 ms, Bazett QTc 488 ms - still borderline but below 500 ms. The prior tracing of 2/2/2020 had a grossly prolonged QT (556 ms) with Bazett QTc 620 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 132 ms (>=60 ms), a substantial improvement. No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block.

Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, perfectly regular (RR 498 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00) with a clear P wave before each QRS; PR 196 ms (upper normal, no AV block). QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +51 degrees (normal). QT 290 ms, QTc 411 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 184 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 413 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and a QTc difference of only 2 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 55/min, regular (RR 1101 ms), with an upright P wave before every QRS. The PR interval is prolonged at about 222 ms with 1:1 conduction - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis about +1 degree (lead I upright, aVF nearly isoelectric) - normal. QT 416 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 51/min with PR 194 ms, QRS 84 ms and QTc 387 ms; there is no new AF/flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of only 10 ms, so no listed change categories apply (the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: no organised atrial activity and irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms); mean ventricular rate about 151/min. No measurable PR interval (null). QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -23 degrees (normal). QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The tracing from the previous evening (9/12/2025) also showed atrial fibrillation, at about 77/min with QTc 434 ms, so the rhythm is unchanged and the QTc difference is only 4 ms; the ventricular rate has accelerated markedly, which is what prompted the intravenous amiodarone given later that day. He is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 72/min with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 174 ms; slight RR variability (RMSSD 35 ms) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +1 degree (normal). QT 364 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 had a markedly prolonged QT (520 ms) with QTc 549 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 150 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. The 11/23/2025 clinic note describing "ECG today: sinus rhythm" is consistent with this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS; PR about 194 ms, at the upper limit of normal but not meeting criteria for first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +54 degrees (normal). QT 388 ms, Bazett QTc 431 ms - normal. The tracing carries some high-frequency noise but the measurements are reliable on the signal-averaged beat. This is the only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, metronomically regular (RR 538 ms, coefficient of variation 0.00), with a discrete upright P wave in II/III/aVF before every QRS (PR 176 ms) - not atrial flutter. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +32 degrees (normal). Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy are met (deep S in V1-V2, tall R in V5-V6) with secondary ST-T changes. QT 314 ms, Bazett QTc 428 ms. The prior tracing of 7/4/2022 was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115/min, PR 180 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 428 ms), so there are no changes. Atrial flutter was coded in September 2025 but is not present on this tracing.

Sinus rhythm at about 62/min with an upright, somewhat broad P wave before each conducted QRS and a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not clearly first-degree AV block). The RR series (984, 984, 540, 1370, 996, 968, 936, 980, 978 ms) shows one early beat with a compensatory pause - an isolated ectopic - on an otherwise regular sinus rhythm; this is not atrial fibrillation, since a consistent P wave precedes each sinus beat. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -35 degrees (positive I and aVL, negative II/III/aVF) - left axis deviation. QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only one ECG is on file. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded at this same encounter, and sinus rhythm on this tracing does not exclude it.

Regular rhythm at 70/min with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS at PR 150 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal plane is highly unusual: QRS is deeply negative in I (-1.4 mV) and II, positive in aVR, and slightly negative in aVF, giving a measured axis of about -172 degrees (EXTREME / north-west quadrant); the P wave is likewise negative in I and aVL and positive in aVR while the precordial leads show entirely normal R-wave progression. This pattern is characteristic of left/right arm electrode reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms - normal (reassuring, since this ECG followed the escitalopram start, although it was done 19 days after the start rather than within the required 14 days). No prior ECG is available.

Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR about 160 ms. QRS 96 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +38 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad, low-amplitude T wave: QT 530 ms at RR 858 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 574 ms - well above 500 ms. The prior tracing of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QTc 442 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 130 ms (>=60 ms). No new AF, flutter, pacing or bundle branch block. Marked QT prolongation in a 35-year-old woman taking citalopram 40 mg daily - flagged separately for urgent prescriber review.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR 878 ms), with a clear upright P wave before each QRS and PR 150 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about +71 degrees (normal, vertical). QT 436 ms, Bazett QTc 465 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold, and acceptable on escitalopram; worth re-checking if the dose is increased or another QT-prolonging drug is added. No prior ECG is on file. This tracing satisfied the 30-day post-escitalopram monitoring requirement.

Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, with an upright P wave before each QRS and PR 182 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -10 degrees (normal). QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms - normal. The prior tracing of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66/min with PR 172 ms, QRS 94 ms and QTc 406 ms; there is no new AF or flutter, no pacing, no new bundle branch block and a QTc difference of about 31 ms, so no change categories apply.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, upright P waves with PR about 150 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +36 degrees (normal). The T wave is markedly prolonged and broad: QT 518 ms at RR 880 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 552 ms - clearly above 500 ms.
